1 - Syntax

import openwillis as ow
words, turns, summary = ow.speech_characteristics(
json_conf='',
language='en',
speaker_label=None,
min_turn_length=1,
min_coherence_turn_length=5,
option='coherence',
feature_groups=None,
)
# Or, when using the subpackage directly:
import openwillis.speech as ows
words, turns, summary = ows.speech_characteristics(
json_conf='',
language='en',
speaker_label=None,
min_turn_length=1,
min_coherence_turn_length=5,
option='coherence',
feature_groups=None,
)
2 - Methods
(cid:127) The function measures speech characteristics from transcript JSON produced by the OpenWillis speech pipeline
(Vosk-like word lists, Whisper segments, or Amazon Transcribe items).
(cid:127) The current implementation always returns three dataframes: `word_df`, `turn_df`, and `summ_df`. Empty outputs
are padded so row `0` still exists.
(cid:127) Pause and repetition branches are language-agnostic in control flow; sentiment, POS, and first-person branches
are currently gated to `language in {'en', 'uk', 'ua'}`.
(cid:127) Coherence features are only attempted when `option='coherence'`, the `feature_groups` selector includes
`coherence`, and the selected backend models load successfully.
(cid:127) The coherence backend is selected by `OPENWILLIS_COHERENCE_BACKEND` and currently supports `gemma`
and `bert`.

code path still builds

(cid:127) `pre_word_pause`: Pause time before each timed word in seconds. The raw inter-word gap is computed from
word timestamps, converted to numeric, and clamped to `>= 0`. The first word in the file is `NaN`; when turn
boundaries are available, the first word of each turn is also reset to `NaN` so turn-start gaps are represented by
`pre_turn_pause` instead of the word column.
(cid:127) `num_syllables`: Number of syllables in the word. The code uses NLTK's `SyllableTokenizer`; Ukrainian (`uk`/`ua`)
uses a custom sonority hierarchy, while every other language code falls back to the default English tokenizer
implementation.
(cid:127) `part_of_speech`: Broad part-of-speech label written at the word level. The current implementation uses spaCy,
not NLTK: English words are mapped from Penn tags to categories such as `Pronoun`, `Verb`, `Adjective`, `Noun`,
`Adverb`, and `Determiner`; Ukrainian uses broad spaCy POS/morphology labels. This branch is only populated for
English and Ukrainian.

(cid:127) `first_person`: Flag marking first-person pronouns/determiners at the word level. The column is `True` only for
tokens whose lowercase form is in the language-specific first-person inventory and whose POS is `Pronoun` or
`DET`; all other rows are set to `NaN`. This branch is only populated for English and Ukrainian.
(cid:127) `verb_tense`: Tense label for verb rows. English uses present/past rules from tag mappings; Ukrainian uses spaCy
morphology (`Tense=Past` / `Pres`) and otherwise falls back to `Other`. Non-verb rows are set to `NaN`. This
branch is only populated for English and Ukrainian.

(cid:127) `word_coherence`, `word_coherence_5`, `word_coherence_10`: Word-level semantic coherence derived from

(cid:127) `word_coherence`, `word_coherence_5`, `word_coherence_10`: Word-level semantic coherence derived from
embedding cosine similarity. `word_coherence` is the similarity to the immediately previous word.
`word_coherence_5` and `word_coherence_10` are local window averages computed from neighbors at increasing
offsets around the current position; edge positions that do not have enough surrounding context are left `NaN`.
These columns are only attempted when `option='coherence'` and the active backend models load.
(cid:127) `word_coherence_variability_2` ... `word_coherence_variability_10`: Semantic similarity to the next word at
distance `k` for `k = 2..10`. Each series is padded with trailing `NaN` values where the required forward context
does not exist. These columns are only attempted when `option='coherence'` and the active backend models load.

2.2 - Per-turn measures

(cid:127) `pre_turn_pause`: Pause before the turn in seconds, taken from the raw pause attached to the first word of that
turn and then clipped to `>= 0` for storage. The first observed turn can remain `NaN` when there is no preceding
timed word. Negative raw gaps are preserved separately in `interrupt_flag`.
(cid:127) `turn_length_minutes`: Elapsed time from the start of the first word in the turn to the end of the last word, divided
by 60. This duration includes both spoken words and within-turn silences.

(cid:127) `turn_length_words`: Number of timed words assigned to the turn.
(cid:127) `words_per_min`: Turn-level speech rate computed as `turn_length_words / turn_length_minutes` whenever the
duration is positive.
(cid:127) `syllables_per_min`: Turn-level articulation rate computed from the syllable count of the turn text divided by
`turn_length_minutes`. The branch uses the

chunks.text:
llables_per_min`: Turn-level articulation rate computed from the syllable count of the turn text divided by
`turn_length_minutes`. The branch uses the same syllable tokenizer logic as `num_syllables`.

(cid:127) `speech_percentage`: Turn-level speech occupancy computed as `100 * (1 - total_nonnegative_pause_seconds /
turn_duration_seconds)`, clamped to `[0, 100]`. Negative pause values are not allowed to inflate the ratio; they are
zeroed before the calculation.
(cid:127) `mean_pause_length`, `pause_variability`: Mean and variance of the positive pause durations inside the turn.
The first raw pause in the turn is treated as the pre-turn boundary and is not mixed into these within-turn pause
statistics.

(cid:127) `sentiment_pos`, `sentiment_neg`, `sentiment_neu`, `sentiment_overall`: Main turn-level sentiment outputs
from the multilingual transformer scorer. `pos`, `neg`, and `neu` are class probabilities; `sentiment_overall` is the
VADER-style normalized compound score returned by the transformer wrapper. In the current pipeline these
columns are only populated for English and Ukrainian.
(cid:127) `sentiment_vader_pos`, `sentiment_vader_neg`, `sentiment_vader_neu`, `sentiment_vader_overall`: Parallel
VADER-style sentiment outputs. English uses the standard `vaderSentiment` analyzer; Ukrainian uses the custom
morphology-aware analyzer in `ukrainian_vader.py`. These columns are only populated for English and Ukrainian.

(cid:127) `mattr_5`, `mattr_10`, `mattr_25`, `mattr_50`, `mattr_100`: Moving-average type-token ratio over several window
sizes. The current code first lemmatizes with spaCy, then runs `LexicalRichness.mattr()` for each configured
window. These columns are only populated for English and Ukrainian.
(cid:127) `first_person_percentage`: Percentage of first-person tokens in the turn. The current implementation divides the
count of first-person pronouns/determiners by the total number of spaCy tokens in the turn, not by the number of
pronouns only. This differs from the older project PDF wording.
(cid:127) `first_person_sentiment_positive`, `first_person_sentiment_negative`: Interaction terms between first-person
usage and sentiment. The current implementation uses `(100 - first_person_percentage) * sentiment_pos` for the
positive column and `first_person_percentage * sentiment_neg` for the negative column.

(cid:127) `first_person_sentiment_positive_vader`, `first_person_sentiment_negative_vader`: Dynamic
VADER-specific first-person interaction columns. They are added to `turn_df` only when VADER sentiment
columns are present, using the same formulas as the main first-person sentiment pair but with VADER `pos` and
`neg` values.
(cid:127) `word_repeat_percentage`, `phrase_repeat_percentage`: Repetition measures after lowercasing and
punctuation stripping. Word repetition uses a sliding window of 10 words; phrase repetition uses a sliding window of
3 phrases. The reported values are window-level percentages averaged across the turn.

(cid:127) `first_order_sentence_tangeniality`, `second_order_sentence_tangeniality`: Phrase-level coherence inside a
turn. The code embeds the phrases detected for the turn and averages cosine si

chunks.text:
, `second_order_sentence_tangeniality`: Phrase-level coherence inside a
turn. The code embeds the phrases detected for the turn and averages cosine similarity across adjacent phrases
(`first_order`) and phrases two steps apart (`second_order`). These columns are only attempted when
`option='coherence'` and a sentence-embedding model is available.
(cid:127) `turn_to_turn_tangeniality`: Similarity between adjacent utterance rows in the filtered turn sequence. The
implementation uses whole-turn embeddings and cosine similarity between consecutive rows in
`utterances_filtered`; in multi-speaker conversations this often approximates response-to-previous-turn similarity,
but the code does not explicitly restrict the previous row to the other speaker.
(cid:127) `semantic_perplexity`, `semantic_perplexity_5`, `semantic_perplexity_11`, `semantic_perplexity_15`:
Backend-specific predictability measures. With Gemma, `semantic_perplexity` is teacher-forced causal-LM
perplexity and the suffix columns use left-context windows of 2, 5, and 7 tokens respectively. With BERT, the same
columns store masked-LM pseudo-perplexity using wide context, then 5-token, 11-token, and 15-token total
windows. These columns are only attempted when `option='coherence'` and the required backend models load.

(cid:127) `interrupt_flag`: Boolean flag for overlapping or interrupted turn boundaries. The current implementation sets the
flag only when the raw pre-turn gap is strictly negative (`< 0`), not when it is exactly zero.

2.3 - Summary

(cid:127) `file_length`: Total file duration in minutes. AWS and Whisper compute this from the maximum segment/item end
time; Vosk-like input uses the end time of the final word.
(cid:127) `speech_length_minutes`: Total speech duration in minutes. When turn rows exist

time; Vosk-like input uses the end time of the final word.
(cid:127) `speech_length_minutes`: Total speech duration in minutes. When turn rows exist, the code sums
`turn_length_minutes`; otherwise it reconstructs speech duration from the first and last timed word in the transcript.
(cid:127) `speech_length_words`: Total number of timed words in the analyzed transcript. When turn rows exist the code
sums `turn_length_words`; otherwise it uses the number of timed words directly.

(cid:127) `words_per_min`, `syllables_per_min`, `speech_percentage`: File-level rate measures. `words_per_min` is
`speech_length_words / speech_length_minutes`. `syllables_per_min` is total syllables divided by
`speech_length_minutes`. Summary `speech_percentage` is `100 * speech_length_minutes / file_length`, so it is
not computed from pause sums in the same way as the turn-level version.
(cid:127) `mean_pre_word_pause`, `mean_pause_variability`: Mean and variance of `pre_word_pause` across the full
`word_df`, skipping `NaN` values.

(cid:127) `sentiment_pos`, `sentiment_neg`, `sentiment_neu`, `sentiment_overall`: Summary transformer sentiment. If
turn-level transformer scores exist, the code aggregates the turn probabilities with token-count weights; the
summary `sentiment_overall` is then computed as `pos - neg` on the weighted probabilities. If turn-level scores are
unavailable, the code falls back to scoring the full transcript string directly.

(cid:127) `sentiment_vader_pos`, `sentiment_vader_neg`, `sentiment_vader_neu`, `sentiment_vader_overall`:
Summary VADER sentiment. Unlike the transformer branch, the current code always scores the full transcript string
directly for the summary VADER columns.
(cid:127) `mattr_5`, `mattr_10`, `mattr_25`, `mattr_50`, `mattr_100`: Summary lexical-diversity measures computed on the
full transcript after spaCy lemmatization.
(cid:127) `first_person_percentage`: First-person token percentage on the full transcript, computed as first-person tokens
divided by all spaCy tokens in the transcript.

(cid:127) `prop_verb_past`, `prop_function_words`: Grammar summary features. `prop_verb_past` is the share of
past-tense verbs among all verbs and auxiliaries. `prop_function_words` is the share of function words (`PRON`,
`DET`, `ADP`, `CCONJ`, `SCONJ`) among all non-space, non-punctuation tokens. These columns are only
populated for English and Ukrainian.
(cid:127) `first_person_sentiment_positive`, `first_person_sentiment_negative`, `first_person_sentiment_overall`:
Summary first-person/sentiment interactions. The positive and negative columns reuse the same formulas as the
turn-level metrics. `first_person_sentiment_overall` then picks the positive or negative interaction depending on
whether sentiment is net positive or net negative; with turn rows present, the code computes that choice per turn
and averages the selected values.

(cid:127) `first_person_sentiment_positive_vader`, `first_person_sentiment_negative_vader`,
`first_person_sentiment_overall_vader`: Dynamic VADER-specific first-person interaction columns. They are
added only when VADER sentiment columns exist and follow the same selection logic as the main summary

3 - Inputs

Input Type Description
`json_conf` JSON; required Transcript JSON from a Vosk-like word list, Whisper segment output,
Amazon Transcribe output, or the equivalent OpenWillis transcription
wrapper.
`language` String; optional, default = Language hint. The current code normalizes it to the first two
`'en'` lowercase characters and uses it to gate sentiment/POS/first-person
features and to select Ukrainian-specific resources.
`speaker_label` String or `None`; Speaker label used to enable turn-level outputs and to compute
optional, default = `None` `speaker_percentage`. In the current implementation it does not fully
restrict turn-level feature extraction to that speaker.
`min_turn_length` Integer; optional, default Minimum number of words required for a turn to participate in
= `1` turn-level feature calculation.
`min_coherence_turn_le Integer; optional, default Minimum number of words required for a turn to participate in
ngth` = `5` word/phrase coherence calculations.

`option` String; optional, default = `'simple'` calculates pause, lexical, sentiment, first-person, and
`'coherence'` repetition branches; `'coherence'` adds coherence and perplexity
features.
`feature_groups` String, sequence, or Optional selector for `pause`, `repetition`, `coherence`, `sentiment`,
`None`; optional, default and `first_person`. If `first_person` is requested, the sentiment
= `None` branch is forced on as well because first-person interaction metrics
depend on sentiment outputs.

`words` / `word_df` pandas.DataFrame Per-word measures such as pauses, syllable counts, POS labels,
first-person flags, verb tense, and word-level coherence series.
